parts.name: Agent plugins
parts.caption: Which hooks each agent runs
parts.description: Small config folders for Claude Code, agy, Codex, Cursor and Copilot. They decide which of the agent's events reach the studio, and each entry names its agent to the hook. `plotkeeper install` renders them with the path of the hook binaries in the data folder's `bin/` and installs them through each agent's own plugin command, or, for Codex and Cursor, which have none, into their user-level hook files.

parts.name: Hook
parts.caption: Records every agent event
parts.description: Runs on each agent event and appends it to the event log, with the agent its entry named; an event of another harness, such as Cursor's on Claude Code's entry, it drops, as that harness's own entry records it. It records no process for an agent that runs inside an IDE app such as VS Code, so such a session goes idle rather than being ended by the process check. It also holds a question or a blocked command until you answer.

parts.name: Core
parts.caption: Turns events into session state
parts.description: Plain Rust logic. It reads the event log's lines in order, each by the agent its line names (Claude Code, agy, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Qwen Code), and knows every session's turns, checks, subagents and whether it needs you.

parts.name: Server
parts.caption: Holds the state, answers the commands
parts.description: A library, and the `plotkeeper` program that serves it, with no window in it. It holds the core state, the card store (which keeps the session briefs, the turn summaries and the cards written before cards were retired), the risk notes, the writer and the settings, tells the page why when the writer fails, lists the writers the login shell finds, keeps the API-key writers' keys in plotkeeper's own Keychain entries (the page learns only whether one is set) and the OpenAI-compatible API's base URL in the settings, and runs the page's Test of one (a pass saves the choice and turns summaries on for a user who arrived with none configured), runs the read loop that follows the event log and sends what changed (the list, the selection, the brief, notices) to a sink the web server sets, serves the learning layer as a local page on 127.0.0.1 (the built page, one POST route for each command and one server-sent event stream, behind a random token, a cookie and a Host check, one server per data folder), refreshes at each start the copies of the hook binaries in the data folder's `bin/` that the hooks run, wires the agents it finds to those hooks with `plotkeeper install` (through `claude plugin`, `agy plugin` and `copilot plugin`, and into `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, which hold no credentials, never opening Claude Code's settings file, after removing the archived app's setup and backing up what it changes) and takes that back with `plotkeeper uninstall`, and has one function for each learning-layer and session-view command: the PR lookups on a turn's end, the page's focus and the Map view's opening (never on a timer), the PR briefs written for ready PRs and kept per head, the map, the fog a PR's reading clears, the CI result it reads from the default branch, which map changes and agent decisions of a PR you accepted or overturned, the quiet log of what you use of it, and the background runs: headless agent runs it starts on your click through a launcher that outlives it, one at a time per project, inside Claude Code's sandbox, with their queue, Cancel and record.

parts.name: Understanding
parts.caption: Writes what you read, and keeps it
parts.description: Decides what a change is worth telling you, asks the writer for it, by running its program or, for an API-key writer, over HTTP, with the reply read the same way on both paths, and stores it: turn summaries, session briefs, PR briefs (the facts, the writer's reply and the code checks on it) and the risk notes of blocked commands. Cards, as a turn's or a worker's explanation, are retired; the cards stored before stay readable.

parts.name: Window
parts.caption: Everything you see and press
parts.description: The page: the list, the rail, Home, History, the Map view and the writer section under Writer, where you pick the program that writes the summaries, with its model and effort, or set up an API-key writer, an Anthropic API key or an OpenAI-compatible API's base URL and optional key, and test it with one tiny call. It shows state and sends your actions to the server; it has no terminals, projects, branches, skills or usage, and every other setting is edited in the settings files.

parts.name: Workbench
parts.caption: Worktrees, PRs and plan usage
parts.description: Git worktrees, tasks, PR lookups and plan usage, and agy's plugin: the shipped `plugin-agy/`, embedded, rendered with the hook's path and installed with `agy plugin`. A black box: it never fogs and never asks for your time.

laws.text: Install and uninstall reach Claude Code only through `claude plugin` and never open its settings file.
The hook never makes the agent wait, except for your answer.
The core does no I/O except reading transcripts.
A check's result is its last run's.
The window's types and the Rust wire types agree.
A session's pieces are written one at a time, in order.
A stored file of an older format still loads.
Replaying the log never rewrites, replaces or deletes a stored card, summary or answer.

A change is untrusted text: the writer has no tools where it can turn them off (Claude; Copilot's empty tool allow-list, from its docs), else it runs read-only (Codex's read-only sandbox, Cursor's ask mode) or as locked as its flags allow (agy's sandboxed terminal, with no slash commands or skills), always in an empty folder.
Loud colour is only for what needs you and for a broken law.

hops.text: Core sees the turn end and the server asks for its summary.
The server passes the request on; understanding queues it for the session.
Understanding asks the writer for the summary, and for the session's Goal and Design so far.
The writer's reply comes back and understanding stores it.
Understanding tells the server the brief changed.
